sections.h2: How does the lake affect selling a house in St. Clair Shores?
sections.html:
Lake St. Clair touches nearly everything about a St. Clair Shores sale, from canal-front and lakefront houses to the flood-zone check that comes with insurance. Close to 19 percent of the city's area is water, and part of the city sits inside the FEMA floodplain, so learn your address's status before you list.

The city is in southern Macomb County, west of the lake and about 14 miles northeast of downtown Detroit. The Census Bureau puts July 2025 population at 57,872. Owners reach buyers three common ways:

  • An agent listing suits a house in good shape and a seller who can wait on a buyer's loan.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale saves the commission and hands you the contract and title work.
  • A cash sale as-is fits deferred repairs, a tenant or an estate. Compare offers and see who pays which closing costs.

sections.h2: What is St. Clair Shores like for a seller?
sections.html:
The city measures 14.40 square miles overall, with 2.72 of them water. Wikipedia reports about 14 miles of canals, most along the Nautical Mile, the Jefferson Avenue strip between 9 Mile and 10 Mile Roads that holds restaurants, boat dealers and marinas. The 28-story Shore Club Sky Tower, at the foot of Nine Mile Road, is the tallest structure in town.

French settlers arrived as early as 1710, and farms dominated until the early 1900s. Residents formed a village in 1925 and voted to become a city in January 1951. Subdivisions platted decades earlier filled in after World War II, and Wikipedia calls the city Detroit's fastest-growing suburb of the 1950s. Jefferson Beach Amusement Park ran on the lakefront from 1927 to 1959.

Youth hockey is a local tradition, with two municipal ice arenas at the civic recreation center. Interstate 94 skirts the western edge through exits 224 to 230, about 13 miles from midtown Detroit.

Population peaked decades ago. The census counted 63,096 residents in 2000, 59,715 in 2010 and 58,874 in 2020, while land density eased from 5,139.5 to 5,040.2 people per square mile between 2010 and 2020. During Prohibition the lakefront village was known for roadhouses and rum running, and the Miss St. Clair Shores scholarship program has run since 1953.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about St. Clair Shores homes?
sections.html:
Among the four cities in the Census comparison table, St. Clair Shores has the top ownership share and the top household income.

The 2020 census counted 28,507 housing units, 4.4 percent of them vacant, and a median age of 44.8 years.

Education and age data fill in the buyer profile: 95.0 percent of adults 25 and older finished high school and 29.7 percent hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Residents under 18 make up 17.6 percent and those 65 and over 22.0 percent. The city counts 2,958 veterans, and 92.2 percent of households have broadband. About 8.4 percent of residents live in poverty.

sections.h2: How does the floodplain affect a St. Clair Shores sale?
sections.html:
FEMA redraws its maps from time to time, according to the city's flood page, so a parcel once inside the floodplain may now sit outside it, and the opposite can happen too. Insurers and lenders commonly look at an address's flood status, so a buyer may ask about it.

The city names two lookup tools:

  • Macomb County GIS: type the address, open Layers, expand Natural Features and tick Flood Zones. A parcel that turns red may be in the zone.
  • FEMA's flood map search by street address.

When an insurer has put the house in the floodplain but you hold a survey or other evidence that says otherwise, the city says you may qualify for a Letter of Map Amendment or can file its Options to Appeal Determination form. Settle this before listing to avoid a surprise during a buyer's loan review.

sections.h2: Which school districts and roads matter to buyers here?
sections.html:
Three public districts share the city. South Lake Schools covers the south, Lakeview Public Schools the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools the north, and each runs a high school inside the city limits. Ask the districts to confirm a specific address, since buyers want that detail.

Private options include St. Isaac Jogues and St. Joan of Arc, while St. Germaine closed in 2024. Wikipedia credits the city's popularity to its lakefront, park system, recreation programs and choice of districts.

I-94 and Jefferson Avenue carry most commuters. The average trip to work is 26.7 minutes, the longest of the four cities in the Census table.

sections.h2: What do St. Clair Shores rules say about rental houses?
sections.html:
The city wants every non-owner-occupied house registered and holding a certificate of approval before anyone moves in. Its registration form prints these terms:

  • Single-family house: $150 for the first 3,000 square feet, then $10 for each added 1,000 square feet.
  • Multiple-family building: $150 for the first unit, then $50 for each added unit in that building.
  • The fee pays for the first inspection and one follow-up. A rescheduled visit when nobody is on site costs $30, and a failed-compliance reinspection costs half the original fee.
  • Owners living outside Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw and St. Clair counties must name a local agent.
  • After a sale, the seller sends a recorded deed or land contract copy to come off the city's records.

Call Community Development and Inspections at 586-447-3340 to confirm what applies to your address and whether any open permit needs closing out before a sale.

sections.h2: What will the Macomb County recorder charge me?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Register of Deeds in Mount Clemens (120 N. Main St.), and the recording fee is $30 whatever the page count, with $4 of it directed to the state survey and remonumentation fund. The office phone is (586) 469-7953.

Warranty deeds, deeds carrying a warranty or covenant clause, land contracts and their assignments need a County Treasurer tax certificate first. The Register's fee page prices that certificate at $5 for as many as five legal descriptions.

The county's transfer tax table multiplies the sale price by 0.0075 for the state and by 0.0011 for the county. Your title company can turn those rates into a dollar total at your price.

Treasury's ownership FAQ adds that the buyer reports the change of ownership to the assessor on Form 2766 inside 45 days.

faqs.q: Is my St. Clair Shores house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Check Macomb County GIS or FEMA's flood map search, both linked by the city. Part of the city is in the FEMA floodplain, and a survey that shows otherwise may support a Letter of Map Amendment.

faqs.q: What do the county recorder and transfer tax cost on a Macomb sale?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per document at the Register of Deeds. The schedule lists the state transfer tax at 0.0075 of the sale price and the county tax at 0.0011.

faqs.q: Must a rental house be registered with St. Clair Shores?
faqs.a: Yes. Registration and a certificate of approval come before occupancy, and the fee for a single-family house begins at $150 for the first 3,000 square feet.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my St. Clair Shores street?
faqs.a: It depends on location: South Lake Schools in the south, Lakeview Public Schools in the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools in the north. Confirm the address with the district.

faqs.q: How large is St. Clair Shores?
faqs.a: Wikipedia gives a total area of 14.40 square miles, with 2.72 of water, and the Census Bureau lists 11.68 square miles of land. The 2020 census counted 58,874 residents.
